journeys.title: Preparing for a routine check-up
journeys.who: Otis, 65, has two lab reports from different labs a year apart.
journeys.goal: See what changed between the two reports, and write down questions before the check-up.
starterQuestions: Which of these results would you like to recheck, and when?

journeys.title: Organising records before seeing a new doctor
journeys.who: Donovan, 64, is moving to a new practice and has a summary, a letter and a lab report.
journeys.goal: Build one tidy list of medicines (current, stopped, unclear) and recent results to bring along.
starterQuestions: Should I keep taking all of the medicines on the current list?

journeys.title: Helping a parent prepare for an appointment
journeys.who: An adult child is helping Santo, 68, make sense of a results printout, a portal message and a visit summary.
journeys.goal: Understand what each paper says, spot repeated tests, and bring a one-page brief to the appointment.
starterQuestions: Is there anything we should bring or do before the next appointment?

Eastgate Health Centre
Patient: Donovan Johns   DOB: January 1, 1961
Visit date: March 22, 2025   Reason: General examination of patient

Vital signs: BP 109/73 mmHg, Pulse 90 /min, Weight 87.7 kg, BMI 30.1 kg/m2

Results from this visit:
  Blood glucose: 70.8 mg/dL (ref 70 to 100)
  Creatinine: 0.9 mg/dL
  Potassium: 4.9 mmol/L
  Carbon dioxide (CO2): 27.6 mmol/L

Your current medications:
  - lisinopril 10 MG, every day
  - simvastatin 20 MG, as needed
  - prasugrel 10 MG
  - losartan potassium 50 MG Oral Tablet, as needed
  - metoprolol succinate 25 MG ER

No longer taking:
  - nitroglycerin 0.4 MG Sublingual Tablet (stopped June 28, 2024)
  - ticagrelor 90 MG (stopped June 29, 2024)
  - Acetaminophen 325 MG Oral Tablet (stopped October 1, 2024)

Previous prescriptions on file:
  - December 13, 2022: Ibuprofen 200 MG

Plan:
  - Diabetic diet
  - Exercise therapy
  - Prescribed activity/exercise education
  - Next appointment: April 5, 2025 (Encounter for check up)

documents.title: Letter from the clinic
documents.text:
Old Mill Community Clinic
Date: March 27, 2025

Re: Donovan Johns, DOB January 1, 1961

Dear colleague,

I saw Donovan on March 22, 2025 for general examination of patient.
He continues on simvastatin 20 mg PRN (as needed).
He is currently taking metoprolol succinate 25 mg ER as needed.
He is currently taking lisinopril 10 mg once a day.
He is currently taking prasugrel 10 mg.
He is no longer taking nitroglycerin 0.4 mg.
He is no longer taking ticagrelor 90 mg.
There is an older prescription for ibuprofen 200 mg from 2022 in the record.
Results today: blood glucose 70.8 mg/dL, urea nitrogen (BUN) 8.1 mg/dL, calcium 9.7 mg/dL.
We discussed the care plan: diabetic diet.
We discussed the care plan: exercise therapy.
We will see him again on April 5, 2025.

Kind regards,
Dr. L. Fournier

rules.raw: {"document_date": {"value": "November 24, 2025", "evidence": "Visit date: November 24, 2025   Reason: General examination of patient"}, "labs": [{"test": "Blood urea nitrogen", "value": "19.7", "unit": "mg/dL", "reference_range": "7-20", "date": null, "evidence": "Blood urea nitrogen: 19.7 mg/dL (ref 7-20)"}, {"test": "Sodium", "value": "140.8", "unit": "mmol/L", "reference_range": null, "date": null, "evidence": "Sodium: 140.8 mmol/L"}, {"test": "Chloride", "value": "106.9", "unit": "mmol/L", "reference_range": "98-107", "date": null, "evidence": "Chloride: 106.9 mmol/L (ref 98-107)"}, {"test": "HbA1c", "value": "6.3", "unit": "%", "reference_range": null, "date": null, "evidence": "HbA1c: 6.3 %"}], "medications": [], "follow_up": []}

config.quant: fp16 weights rounded to the q4f16_1 grid (model/q4grid.py), frozen; fp16 compute
config.loss: cross-entropy on completion tokens only (JSON answer + <|im_end|>)

browser.docs: data/processed/test40.jsonl (first 5 test docs of each layout, 40 docs)

notes: The fine-tuned model is the browser-ready version: it was trained on Qwen3-1.7B weights rounded to 4 bits exactly the way the browser rounds them, and these numbers come from that rounded model run in Python. In Chrome it gives the same answers on 36 of 40 test documents and the same scores.
The original model is shown at its stronger 4-bit setting (nf4). With the browser's rounding, which is what the app runs live, it does worse: all-facts F1 0.634 on the test set instead of 0.820.

An earlier fine-tune trained on the nf4 weights (final) scored about the same on the test set (0.992) and better on the challenge set (0.930 vs 0.857, though with 20 documents the 95% interval for the difference crosses zero), but it broke when converted for the browser, so it is not the one shown.
All models get the same prompt, greedy decoding and a 1,024-token limit.

Latency and memory are from a Kaggle T4 at batch size 16, not from a browser. The browser-rounded models use more memory here only because Python keeps the rounded weights in 16-bit; the browser stores them in 4-bit (about 0.9 GB). In Chrome on a GTX 1650 the fine-tuned model takes about 32 s per document.

Rules only attempt lab rows and the document date, so they have no all-facts, medicine or follow-up score. Their test-name dictionary is the same list the synthetic templates use, which flatters them on this data.
